definitions.explanation: The continent surrounding the South Pole. Used when the landmass itself is meant, as distinct from {南極|なんきょく}, which can refer more loosely to the South Pole or the Antarctic region.

examples.japanese: {南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}は{氷|こおり}に{覆|おお}われている。
{南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}には{国境|こっきょう}がない。
examples.english: There are no national borders on the Antarctic continent.

examples.japanese: {南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}の{氷|こおり}が{溶|と}けると、{海面|かいめん}が{大|おお}きく{上|あ}がると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that if the ice of Antarctica melts, sea levels will rise significantly.

notes:
Formed from {南極|なんきょく} (South Pole, the Antarctic) plus {大陸|たいりく} (continent).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}に{上陸|じょうりく}する: to land on the Antarctic continent
- {南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}{横断|おうだん}: crossing Antarctica
- {南極大陸|なんきょくたいりく}の{氷床|ひょうしょう}: the Antarctic ice sheet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {南極|なんきょく}: the South Pole; the Antarctic — used for the point, the region, or loosely for the continent
- {北極|ほっきょく}: the Arctic — note that there is no {北極大陸|ほっきょくたいりく}, since the Arctic is ocean rather than land
